title: Xi pushes 'Greater BRICS' economic ties to give bloc larger global role
gist: At the New Delhi BRICS summit, Xi Jinping unveiled a 'Greater BRICS Initiative' built on concrete industrial plumbing - a China-led BRICS AI Open Source Zone, a BRICS Special Economic Zone partnership and a BRICS Service Trade Forum - while the bloc, now including Iran and the UAE, forged a joint declaration on Middle East escalation despite an active Gulf war.

insights.claim: Xi Jinping told the BRICS summit in New Delhi that China will take the lead in establishing a BRICS AI Open Source Zone to promote cooperation on large language models, AI training and an open AI ecosystem.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: China is trying to set the default open-weight AI stack for the Global South, a direct challenge to US model and chip export leverage; watch which BRICS states adopt Chinese model families.
insights.quote: China will take the lead in establishing aBRICS AI Open Source Zone to promote cooperation on large language models, AI training and an open AI ecosystem
insights.locator: China will take the lead in establishing a BRICS AI Open Source Zone

insights.claim: Xi proposed a BRICS Special Economic Zone partnership and said China would host a BRICS Service Trade Forum next year, extending the bloc from communique diplomacy into physical trade and investment infrastructure.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: SEZ linkages and services-trade plumbing are the mechanisms that would make intra-BRICS trade substitutable for Western trade; they are the metric to track, not summit rhetoric.
insights.locator: He also proposed a BRICS Special Economic Zone partnership

insights.claim: Xi framed the success of the 'Greater BRICS Initiative' as dependent on pragmatic cooperation, supply-chain stability and cultivating an integrated market rather than on political declarations.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: Beijing's stated test of BRICS success is supply-chain integration, which implies continued Chinese capital deployment into member-state logistics and industrial capacity.
insights.quote: 'Greater BRICS' nations should further co-operate, maintain the stability of industrial and supply chains, and cultivate an integrated market
insights.locator: The success of the "Greater BRICS Initiative" depends on laying a solid foundation

insights.claim: Beijing is positioning BRICS as a practical platform for Global South development, a reframing away from the bloc's original identity as a counterweight to US-dominated order.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: A development-platform framing broadens BRICS appeal to non-aligned states that would resist an explicitly anti-US bloc, expanding China's reachable market.
insights.locator: as Beijing seeks to weld the grouping into a practical platform

insights.claim: BRICS has expanded beyond Brazil, Russia, India, China and South Africa to include Iran, Indonesia, Egypt, Ethiopia and the United Arab Emirates, plus 10 partner countries across Asia, Africa, Latin America and the Middle East.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: The expanded membership puts major oil exporters and chokepoint states inside one forum, giving the bloc real leverage over energy and shipping narratives.
insights.locator: BRICS has expanded to include Iran, Indonesia, Egypt, Ethiopia and the United Arab Emirates

insights.claim: India chairs BRICS in 2026 and China chairs in 2027, and both are explicitly seeking wider partnership to boost the grouping's global clout.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: Back-to-back India-then-China chairmanships mean two more years of institutional build-out; the 2027 Chinese chair year is the likely venue for the most concrete initiatives.
insights.locator: with 2026 chair India and 2027 chair China

insights.claim: China and Russia are the ones who refer to the enlarged bloc as 'Greater BRICS', indicating the expansion branding is driven by Beijing and Moscow rather than by India or Brazil.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: The naming asymmetry is a tell that BRICS enlargement serves Chinese and Russian strategy more than Indian interests, capping how far India will let it go.
insights.quote: China and Russia sometimes refer to this larger bloc as "Greater BRICS"
insights.locator: China and Russia sometimes refer to this larger bloc

themes.theme: Competing visions from Modi and Putin

insights.claim: Narendra Modi argued that BRICS-developed solutions should not stay limited to BRICS but be made adaptable and accessible for the wider Global South, a deliberately non-exclusionary framing.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: Modi's open framing keeps India's multi-alignment intact and signals New Delhi will resist turning BRICS into a closed anti-Western club.
insights.locator: The benefits of solutions developed within BRICS should not stay limited

insights.claim: Vladimir Putin called BRICS a powerful driving force toward a new, fairer and multipolar world order and urged members to combine the competitive advantages of their individual economies.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: Moscow continues to sell BRICS as an order-replacement project, which is the framing most likely to trigger Western secondary-sanctions responses against bloc mechanisms.
insights.locator: Russian President Vladimir Putin called BRICS a powerful driving force

themes.theme: Gulf war shadow over the summit

insights.claim: The BRICS summit convened amid renewed Gulf fighting, with tit-for-tat US-Iran attacks and Iran-backed Houthis widening the conflict by striking Saudi Arabia.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: Escalation that reaches Saudi territory puts the world's largest crude exporter directly in the firing line, a first-order risk for oil supply assumptions.
insights.locator: The summit comes amid renewed fighting in the Gulf region

insights.claim: The summit forged consensus on a joint declaration backed by both Iran and the UAE - two states on opposite sides of the current conflict - which expressed deep concern over Middle East escalation and urged maximum restraint.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: Iran and the UAE signing the same text while the UAE has suspended ties with Tehran shows BRICS functioning as a de-escalation channel that Western forums currently lack.
insights.locator: it managed to forge consensus on a joint declaration backed by Iran and the UAE

insights.claim: Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian met the Crown Prince of Abu Dhabi on the summit sidelines, the highest-level meeting between the two countries' officials since the conflict began, covering de-escalation and regional stability.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: A first high-level Iran-UAE contact since the war started is an early de-escalation signal worth watching as a potential inflection for oil risk premium and Gulf shipping insurance.
insights.locator: Separately, Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian also met the Crown Prince of Abu Dhabi
